source.title: Reliable extrapolation of deep neural operators informed by physics or sparse observations
source.authors: Min Zhu; Han-Di Zhang; Anran Jiao; G. Karniadakis; Lu Lu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures DeepONet test error across network width, training iterations, and training-set size. It reports U-shaped width and iteration curves rather than double descent, and reports lower test error with more training data.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own width, iteration, and training-data-size sweeps in Section 2.5. Curve values are presented in figures without extractable numeric values, so the rows use figure only. Double-descent results cited from other work, and activation-function comparisons, are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps DeepONet width (1–500), training iterations (to 5×10^5) and training-set size (10–2000) on a diffusion-reaction operator-learning task. It reports test-error curve shapes for each, so it bears on V1–V3 in a new setting: operator learning, mostly extrapolation, no label noise. It does not reproduce the original setups and does not show the sweeps reach an interpolation threshold. T3 fits better than T5: the authors do not argue the versions are wrong and attribute the missing second descent to limited capacity.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find U-shaped test-error curves over network width and training iterations for both interpolation and Ex.+ extrapolation, with Ex.+ showing larger error and an earlier transition point. Larger training sets help both interpolation and extrapolation. They did not observe double descent and suggest model capacity was too small. They state double descent may appear at larger capacity and leave this to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps DeepONet width, training iterations, and dataset size in operator-learning extrapolation experiments; it does not reproduce the original double-descent setups.
record.method_sensitivity: The width-sweep transition point occurs earlier for extrapolation than interpolation and earlier for smaller ltest; error during training is larger for smaller ltest. Improvement from increasing dataset size diminishes as dataset size grows.
record.problems: The relevant curves are presented in figures without tabulated numeric values. The authors state that model capacity may not be large enough to expose double descent; the size sweep uses DeepONets on one equation setting and does not establish behavior near a just-fit training threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant measured outcomes were omitted. Cited double-descent findings and the paper's activation-function comparisons were not included because they do not report outcomes for the claim versions.

untested.parts: Whether test error falls again beyond the interpolation threshold. The study does not show width 500 reaches or passes the size that just fits 100 training functions. Other deep-network classes and label-noise settings are also untested.
Epoch-wise behaviour for larger models or with label noise, where the original reports the effect. Whether training long enough would produce a second descent.
Whether the data-size sweep at width 100 passes near an interpolation threshold, where V3 predicts harm.
Not tested. There is no label-noise or regularization sweep tied to the peak.

missing.what: Test-error curves over training iterations for different activation functions, standard and L-LAAF. GELU shows overfitting after some iterations; no second descent is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' states were changed from absent/reversed to partial (V1, V2) and absent (V3). The verdicts were downgraded from challenges to limits_scope, because the study does not establish that its sweeps reach the interpolation threshold and the authors themselves attribute the null result to insufficient capacity. The curves are figure-only; no numeric values are given.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests network width for DeepONets on a diffusion-reaction equation, but does not establish behavior across deep-network classes or show that a peak occurs near the size that just fits the training set. The authors say capacity may not be large enough to observe a second descent.
The study tests error over training iterations for DeepONets, but does not show a second descent or establish that the tested range reaches the relevant capacity or fitting threshold.
The study tests training-set size at fixed settings, but does not establish that the sweep is near an interpolation threshold or a peak in test error.
No test of whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
No test of peak dependence on label noise or regularization, multiple descent peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No test of whether an effective parameter count converts the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

statements.correction: Width 100; training-set sizes 10–2000; ltrain=0.5; ltest=0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7; larger training datasets yield smaller test errors with diminishing improvement; proximity to the interpolation threshold is not established; V3 verdict: none.
statements.problem: The monotonic data trend is supported, but an unestablished interpolation threshold does not justify limits_scope for the threshold-conditioned V3 claim.
